prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop composition variation for the Helios Alpha documentation homepage
Primary request: Keep the approved Annotated Event Atlas world, but make the first viewport read like a guided research argument from event hypothesis to restartable computation.
Scene/backdrop: a bright contemporary quantitative research atlas translated into a web interface.
Structure: a narrow vertical chapter rail on the far left; a large editorial thesis and one primary action in the upper-left; a monumental aligned-time plot crossing the center and right with ruled callouts pinned directly to t=0, confidence bands, and recovery; beneath the plot, one compact three-step composition strip labeled DEFINE EVENT, ACCUMULATE STATE, EMIT SIGNAL and a checkpoint proof stamp at the far right.
Subject: a synthetic rare-event response curve, event definition, online moments, signal emission, and a versioned checkpoint represented as inspectable evidence.
Style/medium: premium editorial web UI comp, scientific atlas fused with an interactive statistical notebook and precise registration language.
Composition/framing: 16:10 landscape desktop viewport; the event plot is the single focal moment; annotations overlap its margins without becoming cards; code and state are secondary but visible before the fold.
Lighting/mood: rigorous, lucid, calm, decisive.
Color palette: cool white #f5f7f4, ink #111b24, indigo #3155a6, oxide #c64a2e, acid chartreuse #b7d93d used sparingly.
Materials/textures: vellum plot overlays, registration marks, ruled annotation margins, technical ink, no photographic texture.
Text (verbatim): "HELIOS ALPHA", "RARE EVENTS, REPLAYABLE EVIDENCE", "Trace one event from arrival to signal without losing causality or state.", "OPEN THE COMPOSITION", "t = 0", "DEFINE EVENT", "ACCUMULATE STATE", "EMIT SIGNAL", "CHECKPOINT VERIFIED", "SYNTHETIC DATA"
Constraints: designed website surface, not a poster or academic paper; readable typography; credible quantitative chart; accessible contrast; no logo; no watermark.
Avoid: application dashboard density, dark trading terminal, candlestick charts, generic SaaS cards, generic VitePress hero, beige nostalgia, gradients, photographic people.
